samples.xml_description:
<module id="signal_generator">
    <description>Implement a Triangle Wave signal generator module that generates a waveform by incrementing and decrementing a 5-bit signal named "wave". The waveform cycles between 0 and 31, which is incremented or decremented by 1.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">5-bit output waveform signal representing the generated waveform.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="state">FSM state variable used for controlling the waveform generation.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <type>sequential_logic</type>
        <description>State register is updated on the positive edge of the clock or the negative edge of the reset signal. Waveform register is also updated on the same clock and reset conditions.</description>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <description>
            The module generates a triangular waveform by incrementing and decrementing a 5-bit signal named "wave". The waveform cycles between 0 and 31, which is incremented or decremented by 1.
            The module includes a register named "state" for controlling the waveform generation and a 5-bit register named "wave" for storing the generated waveform.
            The state and wave registers are updated in the always block, triggered on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n).
            On reset, the state register is cleared to 0, and the wave register is set to 0.
            The waveform generation is controlled using a case statement based on the current state:
            - In case 0: The waveform is incremented by 1 if it is not equal to 31 (wave != 31). Otherwise, the state is transitioned to 1.
            - In case 1: The waveform is decremented by 1 if it is not equal to 0 (wave != 0). Otherwise, the state is transitioned back to 0.
            The waveform generation continues to cycle between 0 and 31 based on the state transitions.
        </description>
    </implementation>
</module>
